title: suix_queryEvents JSON-RPC params are in wrong order — discovery silently broken
description: discoverVaultsTick builds the JSON-RPC params as [query, { descending: false, limit: 50 }, cursor]. The actual suix_queryEvents JSON-RPC contract (and the SDK 2.x client confirmed at @mysten/sui/dist/jsonRpc/client.mjs:413-419) is positional: [query, cursor, limit, descending: bool]. The keeper passes the options object in the cursor slot, the cursor (when present) in the limit slot, and never passes the descending boolean. On the live sandbox this either errors out (params type mismatch) or returns an arbitrary subset of events depending on RPC tolerance, and the cursor is never honored — so AC3.8's 'discovers vaults' end-to-end path does not work against a real node, even though the unit tests pass (the network-shape test mocks the response and ignores params shape).
impact: AC3.8 fails end-to-end. The Cycle 4 contract's verification — 'with the keeper running, an operator … calls create_vault, and observes a vault_discovered line in the keeper's stdout within one polling interval' — will not happen against the real sandbox. Cycle 5's UI flow (E-007 promotion) breaks at step 3.
recommendation: Use positional order: `params: [{ MoveModule: { package, module: 'tpsl_vault' } }, cursorRef.cursor, 50, false]`. Alternatively, use `MoveEventType` filter targeting `${TPSL_VAULT_PACKAGE_ID}::tpsl_vault::VaultCreated` (also a one-arg query). Confirmed against @mysten/sui 2.16's transport.request shape.

title: Vault registry never resolves baseCoinType / quoteCoinType — trigger loop is dead
description: discoverVaultsTick calls parseVaultCreatedEvent and registry.addOrUpdate with the raw event-derived KnownVault (vaultRegistry.ts:97-106). That record has baseCoinType / quoteCoinType undefined (they are `?:` optional and the parser never sets them). The trigger loop in runOnePollCycle skips every vault that lacks these fields: `for (const vault of registry.iterate()) { if (!vault.baseCoinType || !vault.quoteCoinType) continue; }`. Result: the keeper discovers vaults, polls Pyth, but NEVER fires a trigger because the type tags needed for the execute_trigger<Base, Quote> call were never resolved from manifest.pools. The contract's 'Implementation guidance > Generic type arguments' explicitly required the keeper to resolve these from manifest.pools[]; the deliverable does not.
impact: AC3.10 fails end-to-end. The keeper observes vaults and prices but the for-loop's `continue` ensures no trigger is ever attempted. This is the exact 'structural fix that doesn't actually wire through' regression the contract's 'No stub pipelines' guidance warned against (Cycle 1 friction-log lesson 2026-04-27T22:55:00Z). Cycle 4 contract's E-007 promotion is therefore non-functional.
recommendation: Implement the `src/manifest.ts` module the contract suggested: at vault discovery, look up `manifest.pools` for the entry whose poolId matches vault.pool_id, then set vault.baseCoinType / vault.quoteCoinType (and quoteDecimals + the per-pool baseP/quoteP oracle ids) before `addOrUpdate`. Without this resolution, the trigger loop is provably dead.
evidence:
for (const vault of registry.iterate()) {
    if (!vault.baseCoinType || !vault.quoteCoinType) continue;

title: Trigger evaluator runs but never builds/submits the transaction in either code path
description: Even if R1-002 were fixed and the for-loop reached the fire branch, runOnePollCycle's only action is `logTriggerAttempt(...)` followed by a comment 'Note: trigger submission requires a signer, which is only available in the full boot path. In runOnePollCycle (test seam), we skip submission.' The main() boot path (lines 293-344) calls `runOnePollCycle` directly — it does NOT pass a signer and does NOT have a separate trigger-submit step. So even in the production path, `signAndSubmitTrigger` and `buildTriggerTransaction` are never invoked. Combined with R1-002, no `trigger_fired` line will ever be emitted. The triggerSubmitter module exists but is dead code.
impact: AC3.10 cannot be satisfied end-to-end. Even with manifest mapping fixed, the keeper logs `trigger_attempt` and stops. No on-chain execute_trigger call happens. The contract's CLI verification step 5 ('Within one KEEPER_POLL_INTERVAL_MS interval after the price update lands, the keeper logs a trigger_attempt followed by a trigger_fired line referencing the vault id and a successful on-chain tx digest') is unreachable.
recommendation: Refactor the trigger-fire branch out of runOnePollCycle into a function that takes a signer + deepCoinId + deepPerTrigger + tpslVaultPackageId; call it from main() with the ephemeral keypair as signer. Tests can pass `signer: undefined` to skip submission OR (better) pass a fake signer to assert the build/submit path is exercised.

title: quoteDecimals hard-coded to 9 — SUI/USDC pool vaults compute wrong current_price
description: runOnePollCycle calls calculateBaseQuotePrice with `quoteDecimals: 9` hard-coded with the comment 'Default SUI decimals; manifest-driven in production'. The sandbox manifest carries TWO pools: DEEP_SUI (quote=SUI, 9 decimals) and SUI_USDC (quote=USDC, 6 decimals). Even if R1-002 is fixed and a SUI_USDC vault is created, the keeper would compute `current_price` with the SUI decimal (9) rather than USDC (6) — a 1000× scaling error that would either spuriously trigger every vault (if the wrong-scaled price exceeds tp_price by orders of magnitude) or silently never trigger (if the wrong scale lands below). Comment promises the manifest-driven path 'in production' but no other code path exists in this deliverable.
impact: AC3.10 wrong for SUI_USDC pool vaults: current_price is off by a factor of 10^3, so TP/SL fire conditions are evaluated against garbage. For DEEP_SUI vaults the value is incidentally correct (SUI is 9 decimals), masking the bug in the live demo path that uses the DEEP/SUI pool.
recommendation: Resolve quoteDecimals from manifest.pools entry on a per-vault basis (alongside R1-002's coin-type resolution). The contract spelled this out in 'Behavior' step 2: '… resolves its pool_id to the pool's base / quote coin types and decimal counts (from the manifest's pools[] entries) …'.

title: All vaults always priced via DEEP-as-base / SUI-as-quote regardless of pool
description: runOnePollCycle picks `baseP = deepPrice; quoteP = suiPrice` for every vault, with the comment 'For now, use DEEP oracle for base and SUI oracle for quote on the DEEP/SUI pool. Full manifest-driven mapping is handled in the manifest module.' For a SUI/USDC vault the base price should be SUI and the quote price should be USDC — but USDC isn't even in the keeper's two-oracle list, and SUI as base / SUI as quote is nonsensical. Even for a Pool<DEEP, SUI> with the inverted side (`side = 1` per the Move enum), the formula here ignores side. The 'manifest module' the comment refers to does not exist in the deliverable's src/.
impact: AC3.10 misfires on any non-DEEP/SUI pool. For the DEEP/SUI pool with side=0 the result is correct, which is why the tests pass and the demo path (DEEP/SUI TP) appears to work. But the keeper as written is single-pair-only despite the Move surface being generic. Combined with R1-002 / R1-004 this means the runtime behavior is either dead or wrong outside one happy path.
recommendation: Resolve per-vault basePriceInfoObjectId / quotePriceInfoObjectId at vault-discovery time from a coin-type → oracle map (DEEP-coin-type → DEEP PIO, SUI-coin-type → SUI PIO; flag USDC as unsupported on this localnet). Use the resolved PIOs when reading prices in the trigger loop.

title: Pyth BCS Option<u64> parse for tp_price/sl_price misses the {None: true} encoding
description: parseOptionU64 treats `null` and `undefined` as None, plus any object with `Some` as Some. Sui's parsedJson encoding for Move Option<u64> (per the suix_queryEvents JSON-RPC response format) sometimes appears as `null` (when the SDK normalizes None) and sometimes as the literal object `{ None: true }` depending on SDK version and event source. The current parser falls through the second branch and returns null only via the catch-all comment 'Treat any other falsy shape as None' — but `{ None: true }` is truthy and a non-null object, so it would actually MATCH the `'Some' in raw` check (no — it wouldn't, but it also wouldn't return null cleanly either; it falls through the second `if`). The comment claim is ambiguous; current branch returns null because `'Some' in {None:true}` is false, so the function returns null at the bottom. That's incidentally correct, but the test fixture only exercises `null` and `{ Some: '<n>' }`. If the running sandbox returns `{ None: true }` (which the SDK does emit for Move Options in some versions), behavior is correct by accident; if it returns the structural enum form `{ Some: 'x' }` for Some / `null` for None it's also fine. The fragility is unlogged.
impact: Risk class is misclassified-vault-fields. If the Sui SDK on the live sandbox uses a tagged-union encoding the parser isn't tested against (e.g., `{ Some: { value: '12345' } }` or a plain string '12345' for u64), tp_price/sl_price end up null when they should not — which silently disables the TP/SL gate for that vault.
recommendation: Run an actual create_vault against the live sandbox, capture the suix_queryEvents response for the VaultCreated event, and pin the exact encoding observed in a fixture (analogous to notes/pyth-shape.md's BCS capture). The test currently uses an assumed shape, not a captured one.

title: discoverVaultsTick swallows malformed events silently — vault_discovered miss is invisible
description: The per-event try/catch catches every error from parseVaultCreatedEvent and discards it without logging. parseVaultCreatedEvent's whole purpose (per T-001 contract) is to throw 'a descriptive error naming the missing key' so the operator can diagnose schema drift. Swallowing those errors means the keeper silently drops events whose shape it doesn't understand, and the operator sees zero vault_discovered lines for an apparently-running keeper.
impact: Diagnosis-impossible failure mode. If the Sui SDK changes the event envelope (e.g. fields go missing on a node upgrade), the keeper drops events with no log. AC3.18 friction-log doctrine is the codebase's cure for this exact class of silent failure.
recommendation: Replace `} catch {` with `} catch (err) { logPythReadFailed(... )` — or better, add a `vault_parse_failed` event to the logger and emit it here with the offending event's id and the error message.

title: Cursor is only updated when nextCursor is truthy — exhausted-page state unhandled
description: discoverVaultsTick only updates cursorRef.cursor when `json.result?.nextCursor` is truthy. When the page is exhausted (nextCursor === null), the cursor is left at its previous value. On the next tick the same query is re-issued and the cursor in the params slot (which is in-memory only) lags behind. Combined with R1-001 (cursor in wrong param slot anyway), the effective behavior on a healthy node is to re-poll the same range every tick — eventually re-emitting vault_discovered for the same vaults if the in-memory map were ever cleared. Not catastrophic since addOrUpdate dedupes, but wasteful.
impact: Wasted RPC calls; potential duplicate processing if registry state is reset.
recommendation: Always update cursorRef.cursor from json.result?.nextCursor (allowing null to also be assigned, signaling 'caught up to head'). The next tick should still query but the implementation can short-circuit when no events arrive.

title: TP/SL precedence in evaluator matches Move correctly — confirmed against Move source
description: Reviewed the TP-then-SL ordering against the Move contract at tpsl_vault.move:147-149: `let tp_met = vault.tp_price.is_some() && current_price >= *vault.tp_price.borrow(); let sl_met = vault.sl_price.is_some() && current_price <= *vault.sl_price.borrow(); assert!(tp_met || sl_met, ETriggerConditionNotMet);`. The Move-side assertion only checks 'either gate met'; it does NOT actually distinguish which one fired. The keeper's evaluator returns 'tp' when both are met, which the test (T-004) pins. Since the Move contract emits a single TriggerFired event regardless and the swap path is the same either way, the keeper's tie-break is observationally indistinguishable from Move's behavior. No correctness bug — the keeper's choice of 'tp' is fine, and the assertion in the test is what 'matches Move' means here (Move evaluates `tp_met` first via short-circuit but does not preserve which one fired). Filed for clarity since the dispatch prompt asked specifically about this.
impact: None — the precedence question has no observable user-facing consequence given the Move contract collapses both branches into a single event.
recommendation: No action required. Optionally add a one-line comment noting that the tie-break is purely a keeper-side log/diagnostic choice (not a Move-observable distinction).

title: BCS sign-handling for price/expo correctly mirrors sandbox market-maker — verified
description: Reviewed parsePriceFromBcs against the canonical sandbox reference at ~/workspace/deepbook-sandbox/sandbox/scripts/market-maker/price-feed.ts:28-41. The 34-byte layout (price.negative byte at offset 0, magnitude u64 LE at 1, conf u64 LE at 9, expo.negative byte at 17, expo.magnitude u64 LE at 18, timestamp u64 LE at 26) matches; the negative-price abort matches; the exponent reconstruction `expoNegative ? -expoMagnitude : expoMagnitude` matches. The notes/pyth-shape.md file documents real captured bytes (DEEP and SUI) and the parser correctly decodes them — the tests use the same captured magnitudes (3_058_022 and 94_371_860) and pass. Sign-bit handling is correct because Pyth's I64 BCS encoding is NOT two's-complement — it's a struct {negative: bool, magnitude: u64}, so the parser doesn't need bit manipulation. The dispatch's concern about 'sign-bit handling for two's-complement at the BCS layer' does not apply: the on-wire encoding sidesteps it entirely.

title: PTB references vault.pool_id correctly via the vault record's stored field
description: Reviewed against the Cycle 3 pool-binding lesson (Move contract enforces `assert!(object::id(pool) == vault.pool_id, EWrongPool)` at tpsl_vault.move:144). buildTriggerTransaction receives `poolId` as an explicit argument (not hard-coded), and its caller path SHOULD pass vault.pool_id. The keeper's runOnePollCycle never gets to the call site (R1-003), but the function signature is correct: poolId is a per-call argument, the type tags come from the vault record, and the call would pass the right pool if invoked. The triggerSubmitter is correct in isolation; only its invocation is missing.
impact: None on the function in isolation; integration is broken via R1-003.
recommendation: When wiring the call site (per R1-003), pass `poolId: vault.pool_id` explicitly — do not look up 'the' pool from a config field.

title: calculateBaseQuotePrice mirrors sandbox formula and handles zero/overflow per contract
description: Verified the formula against the sandbox market-maker (~/workspace/deepbook-sandbox/sandbox/scripts/market-maker/price-feed.ts:127-139). Both branches of the scaledExpo sign check match; the zero-magnitude throw matches the sandbox's defensive check (which logs and returns null instead of throwing — the keeper goes one step further by aborting, which the contract's tests pin and is consistent with the Move contract receiving u64 — there is no 'sentinel zero' in the protocol). The U64_MAX overflow check is keeper-only (sandbox uses bigint without bounds) and is correct because Move's current_price arg is u64; passing > 2^64-1 would be a silent BigInt-to-bytes truncation in tx.pure.u64() were the check absent. No correctness issue.

title: Vault registry preserves triggered flag across addOrUpdate but cannot recover from re-discovery without re-seed
description: addOrUpdate preserves the existing triggered flag when the vault is already known. Good. But on a fresh keeper start, parseVaultCreatedEvent sets triggered=false unconditionally (vaultRegistry.ts:106), and the contract's 'Vault triggered ground-truth on restart' decision (#3) requires seedTriggeredFromChain to be called for each known vault before the trigger loop runs. The discoverVaultsTick at index.ts:266-282 calls addOrUpdate but never calls seedTriggeredFromChain. main()'s boot path (index.ts:293-344) also does not call it — there's no per-vault seed step before the loop. Result: a keeper restart immediately after a fire enters a doomed retry loop until the on-chain abort lands.
impact: On restart-after-fire, the keeper will issue a doomed execute_trigger that aborts with EVaultTriggered=1002. The keeper logs trigger_failed (which is at least visible) and continues; the next poll repeats the doomed call. AC3.10 gas-waste, but no protocol-level damage.
recommendation: After addOrUpdate(... wasNew=true), call `await registry.seedTriggeredFromChain(vault.vault_id, getObject)` before logging vault_discovered (or as part of the discovery tick). The seed function exists; it's just never invoked.
